description: Source-lore pass 62 exports the opening sky-ecology material: the Grays, airborne plankton plants, natural levitation adaptations, buoyant secretions, sky-magic lifeforms, and aerial resource collection. Direct manuscript material is source-faithful; all game mechanics are labeled setting-derived.

entries.title: The Living Skies of Kaysender
entries.summary: Kaysender's atmosphere supports floating plants, microscopic organisms, naturally levitating animals, and beings partly composed of magical fields.
body: Kaysender's skies form a living environment rather than empty space between islands. Wind, magic, drifting plant life, floating organisms, predators, prey, and companion species create complete airborne food webs.

Some species fly through wings strengthened by magic. Others use specialized glands, internal fluids, enchanted tissues, or surrounding energy fields to reduce effective weight, control altitude, and bend the air around them.

The lower atmosphere supports tiny organisms called the Grays, living among plankton-like plants that draw nourishment from arcane energy in clouds. Larger creatures may produce buoyant fluids, magical particles, valuable oils, rare feathers, or other potent materials.

sections.heading: Natural Levitation
body: Natural levitation appears through biological fluids, enchanted structures, and surrounding arcane fields rather than one universal mechanism.

sections.heading: Atmospheric Magic Fields
body: Some creatures release magical particles absorbed by the environment, strengthening local fields that assist levitation. Other beings draw directly from ethereal atmospheric forces and are partly composed of those forces.

sections.heading: Ecological and Cultural Value
body: Sky species may be protected, domesticated, revered, feared, or collected for useful oils, feathers, secretions, and magical residues. Removing them can also destabilize local currents and food webs.

entries.title: The Grays
entries.summary: Tiny floating organisms inhabit the lower atmosphere among drifting magical plankton and form part of the foundational airborne food web.
body: The Grays are tiny floating organisms found in Kaysender's lower atmosphere. They live among plankton-like plants suspended in the air and occupy an ecological role rather than an intelligent or humanoid one.

The manuscript does not define their anatomy, reproduction, lifespan, or exact behavior. The complete swarm profile below is therefore setting-derived and exists only to make Gray blooms usable in play.

statBlocks.title: Gray Bloom Swarm
specialAttacks: Arcane Irritation (Ex): Fortitude DC 12 or dazzled and -2 on Concentration checks for 1 round.
specialQualities: Fast healing 1 while inside airborne plankton
statBlocks.environment: Lower atmosphere, magical cloud fields, drifting plankton blooms
tactics: Does not pursue beyond a plankton bloom.
conversionNotes: All combat values are setting-derived because the source establishes only tiny floating organisms among airborne plankton.

entries.title: Airborne Plankton Plants
entries.summary: Tiny plants drift through magical clouds, drawing sustenance from arcane energy and supporting lower-atmosphere ecosystems.
body: These plankton-like plants grow without ordinary soil. Their delicate root structures draw nourishment from arcane energy permeating clouds and surrounding air.
Blooms move with wind and weather and support Grays, small aerial herbivores, and larger filter-feeding creatures.

operationalProfile.visibility: Dense blooms reduce visibility to 60 ft.
effects: Supports Gray blooms and aerial herbivores
operationalProfile.collection: Survival or Profession (aerial collector) DC 15 per hour yields 1d4 units of usable biomass.
operationalProfile.depletion: Collecting more than one-quarter of a bloom imposes -4 on future local foraging and may collapse Gray populations.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Kaysender An introduction / Airborne Plankton Plants

entries.title: Natural Levitation Fluids and Organs
entries.summary: Some aerial creatures remain aloft through biological fluids, specialized glands, enchanted tissues, or internal structures that reduce effective weight.
body: The source identifies natural levitation fluid and specialized internal structures as common adaptations among sky-dwelling creatures.
These living components vary by species and may lose charge or stability after removal. The rules below provide a general component framework without asserting one universal anatomy.

itemMechanics.collectionDC: Heal, Survival, or Craft (alchemy) DC 18 for Small or smaller, 22 for Medium-Large, 26 for Huge or larger
itemMechanics.preservation: Stable for 8 hours untreated, 7 days in preservative, or indefinitely in a sealed arcane vessel
uses: One unit grants feather fall to one Medium creature for 10 minutes.
Four units halve the effective weight of 500 lb. of cargo for 1 hour.
A masterwork installation provides a vehicle 10 ft. emergency lift for 1d4 rounds after propulsion loss.
failureStates: Poor preservation causes loss of effect.
Collection failure by 5 or more releases unstable lift and raises loose objects 20 ft. for 1 round.
Overloaded installations impose -4 on control checks.
itemMechanics.marketValue: 100 gp per intact Small unit, approximately x4 per size category
itemMechanics.editorNote: The adaptation is source-faithful; all values are setting-derived.

entries.title: Buoyant Secretions and Magical Particles
entries.summary: Certain aerial birds and insects produce viscous lift-bearing substances or release magical particles that regulate altitude and enrich local levitation fields.
body: Some aerial species possess glands that produce viscous buoyant substances, allowing controlled drifting and altitude adjustment.
Other species release magical particles absorbed by the environment, creating or strengthening fields that assist levitation.

itemMechanics.yield: 1d3 doses per suitable Small or Medium creature; +1 dose per larger size category
itemMechanics.buoyantGel: Applied to 100 lb. of material, halves effective weight for 1 hour. On a creature, grants +5 on Jump and reduces falling damage by 20 ft.
itemMechanics.levitationResidue: One dose creates a 10-ft. cube of weak lift for 10 minutes, floating unattended objects under 10 lb. and granting +2 on Fly checks.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Kaysender An introduction / Buoyant Secretions and Magical Particles

entries.title: Sky-Magic Lifeforms
entries.summary: Some beings draw life directly from atmospheric magic and are partly composed of the same fields that sustain them.
body: Some aerial beings tap directly into ethereal forces permeating the atmosphere. Their spirits or bodies may be partly composed of magical fields, making them inherently bound to the sky.
Such entities may manipulate winds, currents, or weather and are consequently revered or feared. The source defines a category rather than one species.

templateEffects: Add Air subtype and a good or perfect fly speed.
No need to breathe while within an active atmospheric magic field.
Gain magical-field sense appropriate to Hit Dice.
Lose 1 hp per Hit Die each hour inside a dead-magic zone unless adapted.
Gain one wind, current, levitation, or weather ability.
operationalProfile.boundaryRule: Every named lifeform requires an individual full stat block and ecology.
operationalProfile.editorNote: The category is source-faithful; template mechanics are setting-derived.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Kaysender An introduction / Beings Bound to Sky Magic

entries.title: Aerial Biological Resource Collection
entries.summary: A complete editor-facing procedure for collecting magical oils, feathers, levitation components, secretions, and atmospheric residues while tracking ecological consequences.
body: The source establishes that sky creatures may produce magical oils, rare feathers, secretions, and other potent substances. This entry makes those materials operational without reducing creatures to simple treasure containers.
Collection can alter food webs and magical fields. Editors should track local depletion as well as immediate yield.

mechanics.depletion: Each major collection adds 1 local Depletion

depletionThresholds.5: migration, predator incursion, or levitation-field failure

mechanics.criticalSuccess: Increase yield by 50% or avoid Depletion
mechanics.criticalFailure: Material is unusable and creates exposure, uncontrolled buoyancy, or magical contamination

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Kaysender An introduction / Valuable Aerial Materials
sourceRefs.notes: Rules derived from the source ecology and material descriptions.
